<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d2ca7079b8bc2ba270b722984da9aaafdca3c795` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6dc30b41661e80161fcfaab5ea5ae9cae9a9db2d` — the merge of head `c3aca48d28cdc925b46533ded7d852e75e1d8b76` into base `d2ca7079b8bc2ba270b722984da9aaafdca3c795`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6dc30b41661e80161fcfaab5ea5ae9cae9a9db2d && git checkout 6dc30b41661e80161fcfaab5ea5ae9cae9a9db2d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d2ca7079b8bc2ba270b722984da9aaafdca3c795 c3aca48d28cdc925b46533ded7d852e75e1d8b76 && git checkout -B drift-repro d2ca7079b8bc2ba270b722984da9aaafdca3c795 && git merge --no-ff c3aca48d28cdc925b46533ded7d852e75e1d8b76

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d2ca7079b8bc2ba270b722984da9aaafdca3c795
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d2ca7079b8bc2ba270b722984da9aaafdca3c795` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c3aca48d28cdc925b46533ded7d852e75e1d8b76`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-storage/src/file-reference-lifecycle.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/file-field-pending-upload.integration.test.ts, .changeset/26479-file-field-pending-upload.md, content/docs/api/plugin-endpoints.mdx + packages/services/service-storage/src/field-file-service.ts (`describeRow`, `storeFile`, `claimFiles`), packages/services/service-storage/src/objects/system-file.object.ts (`status`), packages/services/service-storage/src/attachment-lifecycle.ts (`createSysFileReapGuard`), packages/services/service-storage/src/attachment-access-hooks.ts (`callerContext`), packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-routes.ts (presigned, complete, chunked, chunked complete), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`insert`, `update`, per-row `beforeInsert`), packages/objectql/src/engine-execution-plumbing.ts (`buildSession`), packages/rest/src/crud-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/batch-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/form-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/data-action-routes.ts, packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts, packages/client/src/index.ts (`storage.upload`), scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs

Read at 2026-10-27T06:55Z: card #26479 (body, triage `6434181544`, claim `6434803082`, dev report `6435670148`), PR #26531 body and 4-file list, the net diff `origin/main...c3aca48d`, and the head's check-runs.

### ① Derived judgments

**The accept-set change the diff makes (one, located).** In `applyCopyOnClaim` (file-reference-lifecycle.ts, the judging loop run by `beforeInsert` and `beforeUpdate` before the driver), a file-field token that resolves to a `sys_file` row the caller may read is now split: `caller && !held && !isCompletedUpload(found)` pushes it to `incomplete`, else to `rows`. A field with any `incomplete` token (and no unreadable one) is refused through the existing `assertNoFileFieldRefused` → `validationFailure`: `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`, one ADR-0114 `invalid_value` entry naming the field label and the file id(s), message ending "Complete the upload, then save again." Nothing is written (the throw is in the before hook) and nothing is stamped (`claimFile` only runs in the after hooks). **Right.** This is exactly the triage ruling's shape (#26043's envelope, located at the field, the remedy in the message).

**Who is refused now that was not before.** A write with a caller (`referencingCallerOf` non-null: a session that is not `isSystem`) that names, in a file/image/avatar/video/audio field, a `sys_file` whose `status` is `pending`, where that row is not already stamped `ref_*` to this exact (object, record, field) slot. Concretely: a client that stored the `fileId` from `/upload/presigned` or `/upload/chunked` into a record before calling the matching completion door. Anonymous callers were already refused for any file value (#25694, `assertAnonymousWriteCarriesNoFile` runs first); unreadable or unknown ids were already refused (#26043, and `fieldRefused` still wins over `incomplete` inside a field, so the unreadable answer names nothing, as before). Nobody else loses a 201: committed files, released (`deleted`) files, and system / context-less writes are untouched. **Right, and correctly scoped to the card.**

**Ordering claim ("after the read check").** Verified: `findReferenceableFile` answers `'refused'` before `isCompletedUpload` is consulted, and the loop breaks on `'refused'`. Across two fields, one unreadable and one pending, both entries are pushed, the pending one naming its file; acceptable, since the caller may read that file. **Right.**

**Dev deviation (1): `committed` and `deleted` both accepted.** `sys_file.status` is a required select of `pending | committed | deleted` (system-file.object.ts). `deleted` is a file that was committed (its bytes verified at `/upload/complete`, #24548) and then released; `claimFile` already revives it (`status: 'committed', deleted_at: null`) and the reap guard un-tombstones a `deleted` row that regained a holder. Once the reaper has actually reclaimed it the row is gone, so a caller's lookup answers `'refused'`. So "not completed" read as "not committed and not released-committed" is the only reading that does not break the existing grace-window revival, and it is the split `describeRow` already uses. **Sound. Not pinned by a test (see ③).**

**Dev deviation (2): a slot resending the pending file it already holds is exempt.** `held = recordId !== null && isSameSlot(found, object, recordId, field)`. `ref_*` is written only by `claimFile` under `SYSTEM_CTX`, so a caller cannot forge it; `isSameSlot` demands all three of `ref_object`, `ref_id`, `ref_field`; `recordId` is null on every insert (so a brand-new record is never "held"), null on a per-row predicate update (where a file token is already refused by `FileFieldBulkWriteError`, #7102), and null when `input.id` lists more than one id. The exemption therefore reaches exactly one state: an existing record re-saving the pending file its own slot already owns, which claims nothing and moves nothing. Pinned by test 8 and by the dev's ablation (anchor x1 → x0 fails exactly that test). **Sound.**

**Every door that writes a file field.** Every record write that reaches the engine runs this one hook pass: `engine.insert` dispatches `beforeInsert` per row (engine.ts 15407, 15489) and `engine.update` dispatches `beforeUpdate` (16942, 17172). Doors read: REST single CRUD (`crud-routes.ts` → `p.createData` / `p.updateData`), REST batch (`batch-routes.ts`), the form door (`form-routes.ts`, anonymous → #25694), data-action and import routes, and the MCP stdio bridge (`stdio-data-bridge.ts` 968 / 1002 write with `resolvePrincipal()`'s context). A write with no `context` at all gets `session: undefined` from `buildSession` and is not judged; that is a programmatic kernel call, not a public door. `IFieldFileService.claimFiles` is a server verb that commits the file itself, not a record write. The `sys_attachment` attach path is the attachments surface, not a file field, outside the card. **Covered; the "one hook pass" claim holds.**

**Public surface.** No export, type, route or error code is added, removed or renamed. The refusal reuses `VALIDATION_FAILED` and the closed `invalid_value` field code. `isCompletedUpload` and `refuseIncompleteUpload` are module-private. The doc paragraph in plugin-endpoints.mdx states the contract as the code enforces it. **Right.**

**Tests.** The eight legs run a real `ObjectQL` on sqlite with `StorageServicePlugin` on the local adapter and the upload doors called as routes; they pin the card's steps 1–4, the post-complete acceptance, the #24548 byte-mismatch case, the update door, batch-whole refusal, `multiple: true` naming only pending ids, and both exemptions. The red-first reading (6 failed / 2 passed with the lifecycle file at base, the two passing being the controls) is consistent with the diff. **Adequate.**

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/26479-file-field-pending-upload.md`: `@objectstack/service-storage: patch`, title with `!`, a line-initial `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, a `**BREAKING**` banner that names the gate (`installFileReferenceHooks`), the before (201) and after (400 VALIDATION_FAILED), who sees it, and the remedy (`POST /api/v1/storage/upload/complete`, then save again). The PR body carries the same two declaration lines and the same banner.

- `patch` is right: AGENTS.md §3 — a non-protocol narrowing ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition. The diff publishes no new key, value or type.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is right: a published accept set (the record write door) refuses a value it took.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: a record's data value is refused, not anything a metadata author writes.
- ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is honest: nothing is removed, renamed or re-shaped; the remedy is a runtime step, not a code rewrite, so the body carries no migration prescription for the gate to contradict. `Check Changeset` (which runs `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base MERGE_BASE` and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`) concluded success on this head.

Gate reading at 2026-10-27T06:55Z: 47 check-runs, 26 success, 0 failure, 10 skipped (UI, Temporal, opt-in harnesses), 11 still in progress: Test Core 1/8–8/8, Build Core, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · workspace. Every changeset, queue-guard, claim, docs-link, lint and spec-liveness gate that has concluded is green. The verdict below stands on what has concluded; the in-progress Test Core and Type Check shards are the lane seat's to read before landing.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Dev deviation (1), read as committed-or-deleted accepted** — answered: sound (①). Not pinned: no test writes a `deleted` row and shows the write is taken and the row revived. The dev's ablation covers only the held-slot term. Low risk (the branch is unchanged code), noted for the lane seat.
2. **Dev deviation (2), held slot exempt** — answered: sound and pinned (①).
3. **Dev deviation (3), report posted on #26479 not #25235** — procedural, answered by the seat's correction; nothing to judge here.
4. **Chunked uploads** — not stated by the dev. The chunked door also leaves the row `pending` (storage-routes.ts 1091) until `POST /upload/chunked/:uploadId/complete` writes `committed` (1384), so a chunked client that claimed before completing is refused by the same term. The envelope's message ("Complete the upload, then save again") covers it; the changeset's remedy sentence names only `/upload/complete`. Answered: the located refusal carries a door-agnostic remedy; the changeset wording is narrower than the refusal. Not blocking; the lane seat may ask for "or `/upload/chunked/:uploadId/complete`" in the changeset.
5. **`open_questions`: []** — none to answer.
6. **out_of_scope finding, carrier none (reap guard reaps a claimed `pending` row's bytes without reading `ref_*`)** — read and confirmed in attachment-lifecycle.ts 637–646: the `pending` branch deletes bytes and confirms with no holder check, unlike the `deleted` branch. After this PR no user write can create a claimed pending row, but rows created before it (and system/seed rows between `storeFile` and `claimFiles`) still can be. Escalated: this deserves its own card rather than "noted, not filed"; it is not this PR's to fix.
7. **System and context-less writes not judged** — answered: required by the seed loader's `storeFile` → record → `claimFiles` order, mirrors the existing read-verdict exemption, and is unreachable from a public door (every door read passes a caller context). Pinned by test 7.
8. **Two derived gate families NOT MEASURED locally (`check:skill-examples`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`)** — neither reads a touched file; both run in CI (Lint and Build Core families), of which the lint families have concluded green and Build Core is in progress.

Reviewed-by: `fable subagent of session_01R1q2xdtYgU6FKrZ7LgjPCC`

**VERDICT: PASS**

| Shape | Draft, base `main`, `Fixes #26479`, one `patch` changeset on `@objectstack/service-storage` with the BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. 4 files, +401/−2, one of them a docs line in `plugin-endpoints.mdx`. |
